description: BIOGAIAX CODE desarrolla GAIA RESILIENCE, una propuesta de innovación científica y tecnológica que integra observación terrestre de NASA, inteligencia agrícola, gestión hídrica y biotecnología. Buscamos transformar datos científicos en estrategias para optimizar las rotaciones de cultivos, fortalecer la resiliencia agrícola y contribuir a la regeneración de suelos, promoviendo sistemas productivos sostenibles y adaptables frente al cambio climático.
summary:
**AGROBIO INTELLIGENCE – BIOGAIAX CODE**

AGROBIO INTELLIGENCE is an open-source agricultural intelligence platform designed for smallholder farmers. Developed for Montalvo, Moquegua, Peru, it responds to NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: *Field Shift – Adapting Farms with NASA Data*.

The platform combines NASA Earth observation data with local agricultural knowledge to help farmers compare crop rotations and estimate irrigation needs.

It integrates four components: GAIA, for crop rotation analysis and water requirements; GAIA SENSE, for local environmental monitoring through IoT sensors; BIOREGEN, for exploring soil regeneration alternatives; and AGRO TRACE, for data transparency and traceability.

Using NASA POWER, SMAP, and Landsat data, the platform aims to support better agricultural decisions. Its future integration with Starlink satellite connectivity could connect remote farming areas and IoT devices, enabling the solution to scale to other agricultural communities.

**AGROBIO INTELLIGENCE connects space data, local knowledge, and satellite connectivity for more resilient agriculture.**
details:
AGROBIO INTELLIGENCE – BIOGAIAX CODE

Project Details | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

What does it do and how does it work?

AGROBIO INTELLIGENCE is an agricultural decision-support platform designed primarily for smallholder farmers. Developed for Montalvo, Moquegua, Peru, it combines NASA Earth observation data, local agricultural knowledge, and environmental monitoring to help farmers compare three crop rotation scenarios, estimate crop water requirements, and explore planting calendars.

Its four components are:

  • GAIA: compares crop rotations and estimates crop water demand using the FAO-56 approach (ETc = ETo × Kc).
  • GAIA SENSE: an IoT prototype for monitoring local temperature, humidity, and atmospheric pressure.
  • BIOREGEN: explores biological and agroecological alternatives for soil regeneration.
  • AGRO TRACE: supports transparent documentation of data sources, assumptions, and methods.

What benefits does it offer and what is its expected impact?

It transforms complex environmental information into practical insights that can help farmers make better-informed crop and irrigation decisions. Its expected impact is to encourage responsible water use, strengthen agricultural resilience, and improve access to useful information for smallholder farming communities.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, and software were used?

The project uses NASA POWER daily climate data (2020–2025, approximately 55 km spatial resolution), SMAP surface soil moisture data, Landsat 8/9, and NASA Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) data.

The GAIA SENSE prototype includes an ESP8266MOD microcontroller with Wi-Fi and MQTT, a DHT11 sensor, an SHT3x-DIS temperature and humidity sensor, a BMP390 atmospheric pressure sensor, and an ATM90E32AS energy-monitoring module.

The team also used ChatGPT for ideation, technical documentation, and coding assistance. The presentation does not specify the programming languages used.

What makes the project creative?

Its innovation is the integration of satellite data, local agricultural knowledge, IoT monitoring, and crop rotation comparison in one platform. It connects information from space with practical decisions in the field.

What factors did the team consider?

The team considered smallholder farmers' needs, water availability, crop calendars, local conditions, data resolution, sensor affordability, and the limitations of satellite estimates. The scenarios are preliminary and require local validation of crop calendars, soil conditions, crop coefficients, and actual water availability.

The project is designed with an open-source and scalable vision. Future Starlink connectivity could connect remote agricultural areas and IoT devices, helping expand the solution to other farming communities. Public code release and Starlink integration are future steps, not completed features.
